title: Missed early mobilisation and ICU-acquired weakness in a mixed intensive care unit: a nested case-control study
subtitle: Bundle adherence as exposure; ICU-acquired weakness as case status
statement: Eighteen months after an early mobilisation bundle began in a 28-bed mixed intensive care unit, mobilisation is documented on 46 percent of eligible patient-days and about a quarter of patients ventilated for more than 48 hours leave with ICU-acquired weakness. The unit wants to know whether missed mobilisation in the first five eligible days is associated with weakness at ICU discharge, using cases and controls from its clinical information system, while two secondary questions from the director (early identification on day 3 and extra ICU days) must not distort the main study.
whoAffected: Adults ventilated for more than 48 hours in the unit, their families, bedside nurses, physiotherapists and intensivists.
whatHurts: ICU-acquired weakness delays recovery and independence for months; missed mobilisation may contribute, but sicker patients are both less mobilised and weaker, which makes the association hard to read.
currentPractice: A bundle with daily readiness screening and mobilisation within 72 hours when safe; documentation spread across several places.
whyNow: Eighteen months of bundle data exist, adherence is poor, and the director wants evidence before investing in more physiotherapy staffing.
constraints: No external funding. Research nurse 2 days per week until August 2027. Data only from the ICU clinical information system and hospital discharge summaries; no new measurements on patients.
patientCenteredGoal: Patients leave intensive care strong enough to recover function, and mobilisation is offered whenever it is safe.
summary: Problem framed as a nested case-control study with two contained secondary questions.
